final_candidates.decision_summary: Conservative Met→Leu swap at a buried low-B-factor HA2 residue with strongly positive ProteinMPNN compatibility, highest ESM-1v plausibility, and Leu present in ~25% of homologs; classic core-packing optimization expected to improve folding stability.

Ala→Val in a hydrophobic core position with positive structure compatibility and Val tolerated in ~11% of homologs; increased buried hydrophobic volume typically stabilizes folding, though near-zero ESM-1v score tempers confidence.

Conservative buried hydrophobic Val→Ile substitution in HA1 with moderate but consistent support from structure compatibility, PLM plausibility, and homolog frequency; low-risk change likely to modestly improve core packing.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 ranking is stable across three independent evidence dimensions and no available tool directly measures folding stability, so additional evidence is unlikely to change the outcome.

history.rationale: A365 lies in the HA2 central coiled-coil core; increasing hydrophobic side-chain volume with Val should improve packing of the stem helices and raise thermal/folding stability.
Ala→Val in the HA2 stem helix region adds hydrophobic packing volume, a classic thermostabilizing strategy for influenza HA; small-to-medium hydrophobic substitution is low-risk for function.

Structure compatibility positive (0.297) and Val tolerated in 11% of homologs; hydrophobic core Ala→Val typically stabilizes. ESM-1v score near zero is a moderate concern but ESM masked-marginals at conserved positions are noisy.
A317 sits near the HA1/HA2 trimer interface; a larger hydrophobe can fill cavity space and strengthen inter-subunit packing without altering electrostatics.
Ala→Val in the HA2 coiled-coil core could improve helical packing and stability; slight overpacking risk keeps it below A365V.
Weak structure score (0.173), near-zero PLM (0.020), and zero Val frequency among 168 homologs — consistently unsupported.

rejection.reason: Weak structure score (0.173), near-zero PLM (0.020), and zero Val frequency among 168 homologs — consistently unsupported.

history.rationale: V26 in the HA1 globular head core; Ile is a conservative, slightly bulkier hydrophobe that often improves core packing while remaining well tolerated evolutionarily.
Val→Ile is a very conservative hydrophobic substitution in the N-terminal region; modest stability gain expected but low risk.
Consistent moderate support across all three tools (structure 0.274, PLM 0.356, MSA 0.065) for a conservative buried hydrophobic swap in HA1; promotes to rank 3.
M444 is in the HA2 membrane-proximal helical bundle; Met->Leu removes oxidation-prone sulfur while preserving hydrophobic packing, aiding environmental persistence.
Met→Leu in HA2 removes an oxidation-prone residue while preserving hydrophobicity, potentially improving environmental persistence.

Best-in-class across all three dimensions: strongly positive ProteinMPNN delta (norm 0.985, buried low-B-factor HA2 residue), highest ESM-1v plausibility (0.575), and Leu seen in 25% of homologs. Conservative Met→Leu core swap is a classic stability-preserving/improving change.
Alternative hydrophobic upgrade at the HA2 coiled-coil core; Ile offers strong packing but with slightly higher steric risk than Val at a densely packed position.
Alternative to A365V at the same site; Ile offers similar hydrophobic bulk but with different side-chain geometry—retained as a backup pending structural evidence.

Highest MSA mutant frequency (0.368) and positive structure score, but ESM-1v plausibility essentially zero (0.0007) raises viability doubt; demoted below A365V to avoid double-counting the same position.
E119 is surface-exposed in HA1; removing a solvent-exposed negative charge could reduce electrostatic frustration, but functional impact is uncertain.

Surface-exposed (B-factor 21) mutation near the receptor-binding region; removing a surface charge is unlikely to improve folding stability and PLM is near zero, so evidence does not justify the stability goal.
